items.title: New details in the noble feud: Was offered a castle and land worth a billion
items.summary: The noble families' feud over the Trolle Ljungby estate in Skåne escalates. The couple accused of having influenced the count should have received a settlement offer with a castle and land to the value of one billion kroner - but turned it down. The battle is now being pushed on to the district court.
items.title_original: Nya uppgifter i adelsfejden: Erbjöds slott och mark till värde av en miljard
items.summary_original: Adelsfamiljernas fejd om Trolle Ljungby gods i Skåne trappas upp. Paret som anklagats för att ha påverkat greven ska ha fått ett förlikningsbud med slott och mark till ett värde av en miljard kronor – men tackat nej. Nu drivs striden vidare till tingsrätten.

items.title: They show why Mendelssohn's "Lobgesang" still survives
items.summary: Mendelssohn's often underestimated orchestration was allowed to shine, but at times the music flowed a little tight, writes DN's Anna Bjermqvist who saw "Lobgesang" at the Berwaldhallen.
items.title_original: De visar varför Mendelssohns ”Lobgesang” fortfarande överlever
items.summary_original: Mendelssohns ofta underskattade orkestrering fick glänsa, men stundtals flödade musiken lite väl stramt, skriver DN:s Anna Bjermqvist som sett ”Lobgesang” på Berwaldhallen.

items.title: Sweden and India broaden and deepen strategic cooperation
items.summary: On 17 May, Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson received Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi in Gothenburg. During the visit, the leaders held bilateral meetings and participated in discussions with European business leaders on innovation, climate and trade. HRH Crown Princess Victoria, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard, and India’s Minister for External Affairs Subrahmanyam Jaishankar also participated in the programme.

items.title: Sweden organises international youth forum on gender equality and democracy in Belarus
items.summary: On 11 May, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, in cooperation with the Stockholm Centre for Eastern European Studies at the Swedish Institute of International Affairs, is organising a conference in Stockholm on youth and gender equality issues for a future democratic Belarus. The forum gathers youth representative of the Belarusian democratic movement and civil society representatives, decision-makers and experts from the EU and Sweden. The aim is to highlight the importance of young people’s political participation to the democratic development of Belarus.

items.title: Government moves forward with assignment on international power cables
items.summary: The Government is now moving forward with an assignment for Svenska kraftnät, Sweden’s power grid authority, that allows for a planned renewal and upgrade of an electricity cable connection to Denmark to be put on hold. At the EU’s meeting of Energy Ministers in March, Swedish Minister for Energy, Business and Industry Ebba Busch announced that Sweden would halt new or upgraded electricity cable connections to continental Europe unless there was a shift in the focus of the legislation being negotiated in the European Commission’s European Grids Package.

items.title: Pål Jonson to take part in EU Foreign Affairs Council defence minister configuration
items.summary: On 12 May, EU defence ministers will meet in Brussels within the framework of the EU Foreign Affairs Council. Continued EU support to Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East and its implications for European defence and security, and strengthening European defence preparedness are on the agenda. Minister for Defence Pål Jonson will represent Sweden at the meeting.
